  • Translation: Benjamin R. Foster

  • Note: The reconstruction here is based on the frequent use of the verb mullû with puluhtu to describe divine fearsomeness (see [RN2721: P, 505-507]).

3

  • N: [en]nessu | ezzetu || abūbu-ma | [ ... ]
  • T: His [pun]ishment furious, the deluge […],
  • L: [en]nessu ← ennettu I, -šu I “sin”; ezzetu ← ezzu I “furious, angry Bab., NA of deity, person, animal, fire, wind”; abūbu-ma ← abūbu I, -ma I “flood, deluge Bab.”
AššNA1 o 3. [en]-nes-su ez-ze-ta a-bu-ba-ma [x x x (x x)]

4

  • N: [k]īnat? | manzaltašu? || ... [ ... ]
  • T: His stance was unchanging, […]
  • L: [k]īnat? ← kânu I “OAkk, Ass. kuānu(m) to be(come) permanent, firm, true”; manzaltašu? ← mazzaztu I, -šu I “M/NB manzaltu, pl. freq. manzalātu”
  • Note: A logogram KI.GUB for tallaktu is not attested (see [RN680: no. 737], [RN2720: 1310-1311], [RN2721: T, 97-99]). The reading tallaktu of the previous editions appears to be based only on a vaguely similar line from Esarhaddon’s inscriptions cited in [RN432: 295]: šarru ša₂ tal-lak-ta-šu₂ a-bu-bu-um-ma ep-še-ta-šu₂ [la]b-bu na-ad-ru. A syllabic reading does not yield any recognisable Akkadian word, and therefore the sequence KI.GUB-ta-šu is here tentatively understood as manzaltašu, “his position”, perhaps in astral sense as the position of Jupiter (see [RN2721: M/1, 228-230]). Note that the homonym manzaltu, “drainage; flow of excrement” is attested with the logogram KI.GUB ([RN2721: M/1, 230]).
AššNA1 o 4. [k]i?-na-at KI.GUB-ta-šu₂ i# x x x [x]

8

  • N: šuttu | munattu || malmališ | šumr[uṣ]āni
  • T: Dreaming and waking [I was] equally wretched.
  • L: šuttu ← šuttu I “pl. šunātu(m) dream š. naṭālu, amāru etc. to have a dream, to…”; munattu ← munattu I “pl. munāmātu morning slumber jB”; malmališ ← malmališ I “correspondingly, equally Bab.”; šumr[uṣ]āni ← marāṣu I, -nim I “to be(come) ill”
  • Note: See [fromebllab0052: 123]: "The preserved NU rules out the restoration šum-r[u-ṣa-ku].
